extracted.intended_audience: institutional eRA Commons administrators and users (SO, AA, AO, BO, PD/PI, reviewers) and IT/account staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for registering institutions, creating and managing eRA Commons accounts, logging in (including InCommon federated and Login.gov flows), assigning roles, and using Commons UI/search features. Focused on institutional administrators and users who perform account setup, affiliation, and basic navigation tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-factor authentication requirement for InCommon Federated accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Your organization must support NIH’s two-factor authentication standards and you must have two-factor authentication enabled for your account to use an InCommon Federated account with eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your InCommon Federated organization does not support NIH’s two-factor authentication standards and you do not have two-factor authentication setup for your organization’s account, you will be required to use Login.gov; see Transitioning To and Using Login.gov. The two-factor authentication process and software varies across InCommon Federated organizations; direct questions to your Organization Administrators. Compliance and contact information: https://auth.nih.gov/CertAuthV3/forms/help/compliancecheckhelp.html.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing Commons with organization credentials (federated login flow)
rubrics_metrics.description: Steps to log in using an InCommon Federated account: navigate to Commons login page, type part of your organization's name in the 'Login with Federated Account' type-ahead field and select it, click Login, get redirected to your organization's login site, enter org credentials and complete two-factor authentication if enabled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the dropdown list is long it is a type-ahead field. The two-factor authentication screens are managed by your organization (not eRA); if you do not know your org credentials or have trouble, contact your organization — the eRA service desk cannot help with the org login screen. After successful org login you are redirected back to eRA Commons and either logged in (if accounts are associated) or prompted to associate your accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-time association of InCommon Federated account with eRA account
rubrics_metrics.description: If eRA determines that your organization account is not associated with your eRA account, you will be prompted to associate via the 'Associate Your eRA Account' screen — this is a one-time process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To associate: enter your eRA Commons User ID and password on the Associate Your eRA Account screen and click Continue. If successful, your eRA account will be associated and you can log in via your InCommon Federated account thereafter without entering your eRA username/password. Read on-screen messages and tips during the process; contact the eRA Service Desk for other issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisites before associating InCommon account
rubrics_metrics.description: Before associating, ensure your eRA Commons account is active, you know your eRA password, you are not using old bookmarked URLs, and you have an active organization account that participates in InCommon with two-factor authentication enabled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure about eRA account status or password, use the 'Forgot Password/Unlock Account' link in the blue INFORMATION box to reset. The eRA Commons URL is https://public.era.nih.gov/commonsplus/. Your organization must support NIH’s two-factor authentication standards and you must have it enabled for your account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not attempt association with a temporary eRA password
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot associate accounts using a system-assigned temporary eRA password; you must change the temporary password to one of your choosing before associating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To change the password: log into Commons with your Commons ID and temporary password; you should be prompted to change it. After changing your eRA password, log back in through the federated login flow to perform association.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot associate with expired or locked eRA password
rubrics_metrics.description: If your eRA account password is expired or your account is locked due to multiple unsuccessful logins, you will not be able to associate accounts until you reset/change the password or unlock the account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For expired password: log into Commons and use the Change Password screen. For locked accounts: click 'Forgot Password/Unlock Account' on the Commons home page to generate a new temporary password, then change it. For other cases, contact the eRA Service Desk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only authorized organizational administrators can create Commons accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Only an organization's eRA Commons administrators (SO, AO, AA, BO as described) can create accounts; individual PIs or other eRA users cannot create their own accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need a new account or help with passwords, contact an SO from your organization; see 'Finding Signing Officials' if you don't have an eRA Commons account or can't login. See role-specific limitations in subsequent entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles permitted to create accounts and their limits
rubrics_metrics.description: SO can create accounts of any role type except IAR; AO, AA, and BO can create many accounts but each has specific exclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SO: Can create accounts of any role type except IAR. AO: Can create all accounts except SO, BO, FCOI, and IAR. AA: Can create all accounts except SO, FCOI, and IAR. BO: Can create all accounts except SO, BO, FCOI, and IAR. Use role definitions sections for full privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search for existing accounts before creating new account (avoid duplicates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before creating a new user, perform a search across organizations (default) to ensure the person does not already have an eRA account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search in Admin > Account Management. By default 'Search only within my organization' is not marked (searches all eRA Commons accounts). Use the percent character (%) as a wildcard. If an existing account is found, affiliate the existing account rather than creating a new one (especially for PIs and scientific roles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Create New Account screen required fields and User ID rule
rubrics_metrics.description: On the Create Account screen all fields except Middle Name are required. The User ID must be unique and is not changeable after account creation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: User Type should default to Commons and Primary Organization defaults to your organization and cannot be changed. The Primary Organization field behavior: if the individual already has a non-administrative account with another organization, search and affiliate instead of creating a new account. Enter contact info including Email and Confirm Email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email for password resets must be an address the user will always have access to
rubrics_metrics.description: The Email field will be used for password resets; it is very important to enter an email that the user will ALWAYS have access to (which might be their personal email).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the email is changed later, password reset emails will go to the new email address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigning roles when creating an account (Add Roles rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must assign at least one role when creating an account; if no role is added, you will get an error when trying to save the new user. Use the + Add Roles button to select roles; some roles conflict and cannot co-exist (e.g., PD/PI and SO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Ctrl+click to select multiple roles (Shift+click for contiguous). The organization defaults to your organization and cannot be changed in the Add Roles popup. If conflicting roles are assigned, an error occurs when saving; you can remove roles on the Create Account screen using the Remove button in the Action column.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-creation notifications and account edits
rubrics_metrics.description: After successful creation, a success message appears and the read-only Account Details screen displays. The new account holder receives two emails: one with a temporary password and one with the user ID. The person can edit personal/contact info using Personal Profile after they log in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If errors occur on create, they are listed at top in a red bar. To change the new account later, click Manage (note: User ID and name cannot be changed when editing; you can edit email, roles, affiliation, or reset password).

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible Create Account errors are displayed at top
rubrics_metrics.description: A red bar appears at the top listing errors if any occur after clicking Create to save a new account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the 'Possible errors' figure and the next section for troubleshooting. Correct the listed errors and retry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing existing eRA user accounts (Admin actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: SO or account administrators can search for existing accounts, click Manage, and perform actions: edit roles, change account email, affiliate/unaffiliate user with organization, reset password (for users within your organization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To edit roles click Add Roles. Be sure to add ONLY scientific (PI, POSTDOC, etc.) OR administrative (SO, AA, etc.) roles to an account, but not both, as they are incompatible. The Affiliate button appears ONLY if the user is NOT currently affiliated with your organization; Unaffiliate appears if they are affiliated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliate existing scientific (non-administrative) accounts instead of creating duplicates
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person already exists and has a PI or other scientific role, affiliate the person to your organization instead of creating a new account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affiliate is used for scientific (research-related) accounts. Administrative accounts cannot be affiliated to another organization in the same way. Use Manage > Affiliate to associate the existing PI account to your organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admin module search result actions
rubrics_metrics.description: When search results appear you can click the linked Name to see Funding Support (including employment history) to help identify users, click Manage to change affiliation/roles/email/reset password, or click Create New Account (enabled only after performing a search).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Funding Support and employment history to disambiguate duplicate names. Affiliate only scientific accounts; Create New Account becomes enabled after you perform the required search step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account role definitions and privileges (user roles list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commons roles determine features and tasks a user can perform. Roles are assigned by an organization's signing official or account administrator except IAR (assigned by a Scientific Review Officer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide lists many roles (AA, AO, ASST, BO, FCOI, FSR, Graduate, IAR, PACR, PI, POSTDOC, Project Personnel, SO, SPONSOR, TRAINEE, Undergraduate) with short descriptions. Agency-specific instructions may limit applicable roles (example: DOC awards only PI, SO, AO, AA, FSR, and IAR are applicable). See role sections for specific privileges (e.g., AA privileges listed: create/modify roles except IAR/FCOI; reset passwords; create affiliations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment format and size requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All attachments should be submitted in PDF format with a maximum size of 6MB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This note applies to attachments uploaded to eRA Commons modules (e.g., application components). Ensure PDFs are within the size limit to avoid upload errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: New UI navigation and responsive behaviors
rubrics_metrics.description: Modules are moving to a streamlined, mobile-friendly UI: header/footer use symbols that dynamically adjust; sections and screens are navigable via dropdowns; on small screens items collapse under icons; actions column may be replaced by an ellipsis (three-dot) menu when three or more actions exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new header uses an Apps menu showing all apps available to the logged-in user. On narrow screens most header items are hidden and pop down when clicking the grid icon. Footer is simplified. Module abbreviation indicates current module. Section names across the top show current section highlighted; clicking reveals dropdown of screens. If screen size is small, app section names collapse under a three-line icon. Actions that apply to table rows may appear in a three-dot menu instead of an Actions column when there are three or more actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard table tools behavior and tips
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables include tools: Filter (instant filtering and highlight), bulk select/select-all, download/print (exports all columns even if hidden), rows-per-page grid tool, column picker (visible columns only until navigation), column sorting by header, page navigation, Back to Top button, toggle switch states, and responsive hiding of columns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filter highlights typed text in the table and updates count as you type. Bulk actions tools allow selecting/deselecting all visible rows. Download exports data from all columns even if not visible. Column picker selection is only in effect until you navigate to another screen. Hidden columns on small screens collapse under a triangle icon in the row; click to reveal hidden columns. Toggle switches can be disabled, enabled-but-off, or enabled-and-on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding NIH grant number structure
rubrics_metrics.description: A grant number is comprised of parts: Application Type, Activity Code, Institute/Center Code, Serial Number, Support Year, and optional Suffix Code (used for supplements, amendments, fellowship institutional allowances, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and suffix meanings: 'A' identifies amendment number (A1 = resubmission); 'S' identifies the revision record and follows the grant year or amendment designation to which additional funds have been awarded; 'X' identifies a fellowship's institutional allowance record and follows grant year or other designation (example: AG 12345-01X1); 'P' indicates a pre-application. D% (where % is a number) marks resubmissions and/or renewal applications withdrawn prior to issuance of a summary statement at the request of the applicant and a subsequent version was submitted. For full decoding see Deciphering-NIH-Application.pdf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching for awards by Awarding Office/IC field
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Awarding Office/IC field to narrow searches to awards granted only by specified agencies/departments/offices/ICs. Click Change Selections to open a popup to drill down and select grantor organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click arrows to drill down; mark checkboxes of grantor organizations to include; Save Selection(s) updates the button to reflect number selected. Tips: Click Select All or Deselect All. Type at least three characters in the popup search box to auto-expand matching grantor organizations and highlight typed text; then click Select All Highlighted to select all matches. Selecting a higher-level organization auto-selects subordinate organizations under it.
